title: Cleaning Telco and Titanic with train-only statistics
prescribes: Fix types, duplicates and outliers deliberately, and compute every imputation statistic on the training split alone -- never on the full dataset.
applied: Coerced TotalCharges, resolved its 11 blanks structurally, collapsed the redundant 'No internet service' level, and imputed Titanic ages from train-only group medians.
narrative: TotalCharges arrives as text because 11 rows are blank. Every one has tenure = [0] -- these accounts have never been billed, so the right fill is 0.0, not the median. Filling with the median would have inserted GBP 1,398 of imaginary billing history into the newest customers, which is precisely the population the model must get right.

The leakage margin is measurable: the median computed on the training split is 1,397.78 against 1,397.47 on the full dataset. The gap is small here, but the discipline is what keeps the test split honest -- and on Titanic, where 19.9% of ages are missing, the same rule matters much more.

7 service columns encode 'No internet service' or 'No phone service' as a third level that means the same thing as 'No'. Collapsing them removes one redundant dummy column each without losing information. 22 exact duplicate customers exist once the ID is dropped, so no de-duplication is needed.

code_excerpt:
# WRONG: statistic computed over train + test
df['TotalCharges'] = df['TotalCharges'].fillna(df['TotalCharges'].median())

# RIGHT: structural zero, and any real imputation fitted on train only
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, stratify=y, random_state=SEED)
X_train['TotalCharges'] = X_train['TotalCharges'].fillna(0.0)   # tenure == 0 -> never billed
age_by_group = train.groupby(['Pclass', 'Sex'])['Age'].median() # fitted on train
test['Age'] = test.apply(lambda r: age_by_group.loc[(r.Pclass, r.Sex)]
                         if pd.isna(r.Age) else r.Age, axis=1)
takeaway: Every missing value here has a reason, and the fix follows the reason -- structural zeros get 0.0, genuinely unknown ages get a train-only group median.
